reason: The sample jars seem like a natural way to collect channel grains for examination.
expectation: I expect to collect a sample that I can inspect, though I don't know what the grains will reveal.

alternatives.reason: Exposing fresh rock also addresses a goal, but I want to examine the channel grains first.

effect: The jars collected channel sediment, which I can now inspect with the hand lens.
reaction: Nothing notable yet; I’m curious what the sediment will show.
reason: The hand lens is a natural next step for examining the collected grains.
expectation: I expect to see details of the grains, though I don’t know what they will reveal.

alternatives.reason: Exposing the rock surface also serves a goal, but I want to finish examining the sediment first.

effect: The rounded pebbles show wear and movement, but their shape alone does not identify what carried them. The remaining goal is to expose fresh rock.
reaction: The distinction between evidence of movement and its cause is interesting.
reason: The hammer is the only available combination and should expose a fresh surface on the ledge.
expectation: I expect to chip the ledge and expose fresh rock, though I don't know what it will reveal.

effect: The hammer produced a dusty rock chip whose grain arrangement needs a smoother surface to inspect.
reaction: I’m curious whether the rock’s grains will relate to the channel pebbles.
reason: The abrasive pad is the only offered combination, and smoothing the chip should expose its internal structure.
expectation: I expect a smoother rock face that can be examined, though I don’t know what its grains will show.

effect: The smoothed chip revealed bands around coarser grains and a pale vein crossing them, completing the rock examination without establishing how the features formed.
reaction: The crossing vein makes me curious about the rock’s history, though the passage leaves that history open.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the channel pebbles was most worthwhile because it distinguished evidence of wear and movement from evidence of what carried them.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting the sediment felt like a straightforward preparation, with little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The rounded pebbles did not by themselves identify what moved them; the fresh rock face also revealed a vein crossing its bands.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: collecting and inspecting the sediment and smoothing the rock chip all had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue because the pebbles and layered rock raise questions about the landscape that remain open.
